subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the M47D20 (BMW-Sourced) across its Land Rover applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The M47D20 appears in two Land Rover applications — the Defender (Td4, 2002–2006) and Freelander 1 (TD4, 2000–2006).

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing chain, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild. The thermostat housing is a known issue — we inspect it thoroughly and replace as standard.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: The M47D20 has several well-documented issue patterns: Cam chain rattle — timing chain noise is a known issue Thermostat housing failure — failure modes include stuck open (runs cold) or stuck closed (overheating) Boost hose failure — pop and lack of boost with hissing/whistling noise; splits can be difficult to see Injector seal leaks — common on higher-mileage examples EGR valve clogging — common on higher-mileage examples Land Rover M47D20 Symptoms That Justify Inspection The following symptoms don't automatically mean the M47D20 requires a rebuild. Proper diagnosis comes first. Cam chain rattle Temperature gauge drops at speed but climbs in traffic (thermostat stuck open) Overheating warnings, boiling sounds, or coolant push (thermostat stuck closed) Pop and lack of boost (boost hose failure) Loss of power

typical.title: LAND ROVER M47D20 (BMW-Sourced) REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: The M47D20 is a BMW-sourced engine, also used in BMW 3 Series and 5 Series of the same era. The thermostat housing failure is common — it can fail stuck open (running cold) or stuck closed (overheating). Boost hoses can split, causing loss of boost; splits can be difficult to see. These are genuine platform characteristics — we inspect for all of them during a full strip-down. A full rebuild also includes thorough inspection of the timing chain, which can develop rattle from wear.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, thermostat housing, boost hoses, injector seals, EGR system
